status: Staged for guide /13 (brief 102, Fable 2026-11-08). No /13 run applies before Sky's yes to briefs/102/fable/index.html.
why: Sky 2026-11-08, on "He bought it. He'll be back, and he knows my face.": "that's exactly the kind of scripting that bugs me. 'I will remember you.' lines etc - so unnatural". A line that tells the player a rule or a consequence fails, whoever says it. The game shows what follows through the world and the HUD.

kept.line: You paid my debt? I'm yours. Say when.
kept.why: Sky kept it. Her yes in her own words: the turn and the call are in it, and nobody explains them.
Sky kept it. It is what police shout, so it tells the player who has arrived without explaining anything.

fail.line: He bought it. He'll be back, and he knows my face.
fail.why: Sky's example: the Mislead's rule (he comes back, and he knows the Scout) put in the Scout's mouth.

fail.line: You said no. You'll remember me.
fail.why: Sky's example: nobody tells a stranger they'll remember them. It is the refusal's rule read out to her face.
Sky's example: remembering is the game's job, never a line.

fail.line: Body stowed. A search could find it.
fail.why: Brief 102's example: the hiding place's rule, said like a tooltip.
Brief 102's example: the desk's next scan, foretold.

fail.line: They'll wake with a sore head.
fail.why: Brief 102's example: the knockout's rule, foretold.

fail.line: Still good for it. I'll remember.
fail.why: Sky's "I will remember you" family, in Inez's mouth.

fail.line: You've put it right again. I won't forget it.
fail.why: "I won't forget" is the same family: the game remembers, and he needn't say so.
Tells the player the witness can name the shooter later; a frightened passer-by says what they see now.

fail.line: No free favours. Next time, my fee goes up.
fail.why: The refusal's rule (a later offer costs more) recited by the guard.

fail.line: Help me once more. Then I'll return the favour.
fail.why: The not-yet rule (one more Help turns him), read out to the Fixer.

fail.line: Even a favour gets reported, I'm afraid.
fail.why: States the rule that a loyal person reports any approach.

fail.line: Keep that. This goes in my log.
fail.why: The report announced. The HUD already shows it on its way.

fail.line: You're reporting us, then. I understand.
fail.why: The outcome read back to the person's face.

fail.line: Too little, then. Let me listen first.
fail.why: Tells the player what to do next (Listen first), said to her face.

fail.line: That's good money. Call when you want the favour.
fail.why: Teaches a Call, and the guard has none.

fail.line: I'll look first, then tell the police.
fail.why: The witness's choice narrated as a plan; nobody says their next two steps aloud.

fail.line: Sorry, one visit a shift. He's had his.
fail.why: The call's rule recited as if it were café policy.
The guard has never seen the cell, and nobody outside it knows the other crew as rivals.

pass.line: No, thanks. I don't take money I can't explain.
pass.why: His reason, in his words. The offer was too small, and no rule is said.

pass.line: Say that again for the officer.
pass.why: A threat he would really make. The report shows on the HUD.

pass.line: Take your hands off a Councillor.
pass.why: His temperament in one breath, said to the man holding him.
What a person shouts. The report that follows is the game's.
A denial people make. There is no rule in it.

pass.line: That car's tailed us all week.
pass.why: News in his own words, from what he has seen.
The waking is shown by the person, not foretold by someone else.

pass.line: I remember them, officer. Here, let me tell you what happened.
pass.why: When an investigator asks, remembering is the answer itself. It is the moment, not a rule foretold.
